the development of new measurement techniques for the characterisation of two- and multi-qubit gates.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for a given two-qubit gate and given architecture, a range of measurements are required to provide an accurate characterisation of gate operation, and to provide a conclusive statement on whether or not gate operation is of a quantum nature.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best single figure measures are those that are most closely related to the gate operation.
the CNOT is a quantum gate, but it is not a unitary operation, and that the CNOT operation is not reversible.
the best measure for the CNOT gate is the fidelity of the whole gate, as measured via process tomography.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most powerful and informative measurements are not necessarily the most complex.
, for a given architecture, there is an optimal measurement strategy, and that the optimal measurement strategy is different for each architecture.
, for a two-qubit quantum gate, the most accurate characterisation is achieved by measuring whole-state and whole-process tomography.
